reference.source: Standard endocrinology and clinical genetics references
clinicalPearls: A rare inherited disorder combining hypoparathyroidism with a distinctive skeletal dysplasia and proportionate short stature
Skeletal features include thickened long-bone cortices with narrowing (stenosis) of the medullary cavity, delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle, and slender tubular bones

Two genetically distinct forms exist: an autosomal recessive type from TBCE variants (often with intellectual disability, seen in Middle Eastern populations) and an autosomal dominant type from FAM111A variants
Hypoparathyroidism presents as hypocalcaemia that may manifest with tetany, carpopedal spasm, or seizures, especially in infancy
Ophthalmic abnormalities such as small eyes and hyperopia and recurrent infections may accompany the phenotype
The TBCE-related form overlaps with hypoparathyroidism-retardation-dysmorphism (Sanjad-Sakati) syndrome, reflecting shared molecular pathology
Diagnosis rests on the combination of biochemical hypoparathyroidism, characteristic radiographic bone changes, and confirmatory genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: Kenny-Caffey syndrome is a monogenic disorder of bone development and parathyroid function. The autosomal recessive form arises from loss-of-function variants in TBCE, which encodes a tubulin-folding cofactor essential for microtubule assembly, disturbing intracellular trafficking and organ development including the parathyroid glands. The autosomal dominant form results from variants in FAM111A, a protein implicated in genome maintenance and possibly parathyroid and skeletal morphogenesis. The net effect is defective or absent parathyroid tissue causing hypoparathyroidism with consequent hypocalcaemia and hyperphosphataemia, together with abnormal endochondral and cortical bone growth producing medullary stenosis, cortical thickening, and short stature.
additionalDifferentials: Autoimmune or surgical hypoparathyroidism with unrelated skeletal disease
Osteopetrosis and other sclerosing bone dysplasias
additionalInvestigations: Serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium and albumin with corrected calcium
Intact parathyroid hormone level (inappropriately low or undetectable relative to hypocalcaemia)
Skeletal survey to demonstrate cortical thickening, medullary stenosis and delayed fontanelle closure
25-hydroxyvitamin D and renal function to contextualise mineral metabolism
Molecular genetic testing of TBCE and FAM111A with pedigree-based family screening
Ophthalmological assessment for microphthalmia and refractive error
redFlags: Acute symptomatic hypocalcaemia with tetany, laryngospasm or seizures requiring urgent correction
Neonatal or infantile presentation with failure to thrive and recurrent infections
Prolonged QT interval on the ECG from hypocalcaemia
Signs of raised intracranial pressure or CNS complications
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the severity of hypocalcaemia control and any associated intellectual impairment or infections, which are more prominent in the recessive TBCE-related form. With careful lifelong management of calcium and vitamin D metabolism, biochemical stability is achievable, though short stature and skeletal changes persist.
pitfalls: Attributing infantile seizures to primary epilepsy rather than checking calcium and parathyroid status
Overlooking the diagnosis when skeletal radiographic clues are subtle or misread as osteopetrosis
Failing to distinguish the recessive and dominant forms, which affects inheritance counselling
Aggressive calcium and vitamin D therapy precipitating hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis if unmonitored
references: GeneReviews / OMIM entries on Kenny-Caffey syndrome
management: Correction of hypocalcaemia with oral calcium and activated vitamin D analogues such as alfacalcidol or calcitriol as the mainstay of hypoparathyroidism management
Intravenous calcium for acute symptomatic hypocalcaemia presenting with tetany, carpopedal spasm or seizures
Careful monitoring of calcium, phosphate, magnesium and urinary calcium to avoid nephrocalcinosis from over-treatment
Consideration of recombinant parathyroid hormone replacement in difficult-to-control hypoparathyroidism
Management of recurrent infections with immune evaluation, particularly in the recessive TBCE-related form
Ophthalmological correction of hyperopia and monitoring for microphthalmia-related complications
Developmental and growth support with paediatric and endocrine multidisciplinary follow-up
Clinical genetics referral and counselling, distinguishing autosomal recessive TBCE from autosomal dominant FAM111A disease to guide family screening
